description: "The Corporation of London, Its Rights and Privileges" by William Ferneley Allen is a historical account written during the mid-19th century. The text explores the intricate rights and duties of the City of London's governing body, focusing on its historical evolution, privileges bestowed through charters, and the ongoing debates surrounding civic reform and authority.
